title: Microsoft Teams: default meeting templates apply admin-chosen meeting settings to new meetings
summary: The documented default-template controls, Teams Premium requirement and roadmap details are supported. The statement that the feature takes no actions on its own goes beyond the documentation; the checklist also names controls missing from the table, and two supporting pages should be cited.

claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: 'The feature automatically applies the configured meeting options when an organiser schedules a meeting.'

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The default-template control is admin-opt-in: no default template is applied until one is configured.
claims.quote: Specifies the ID of the meeting template to be applied by default to ad-hoc or standard meetings created by the user. Must use the `customtemplate_<GUID>` format. When set to null, no default template is applied.

claims.where: controls[0].ui
claims.claim: The default-template control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting template policies > policy > template > Set as default.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Meeting template policies.
2. Select an existing policy or create a new one.
3. In the list of templates, choose the custom template you want to set as the default, and then select Set as default.

claims.where: controls[0].api
claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTeamsMeetingTemplatePermissionPolicy -Identity <policy name> -DefaultMeetingTemplateId customtemplate_<GUID> to set the default.
claims.quote:
Set-CsTeamsMeetingTemplatePermissionPolicy -Identity Foobar -DefaultMeetingTemplateId "customtemplate_9ab0014a-bba4-4ad6-b816-0b42104b5056"
Sets the default meeting template that is automatically applied to ad-hoc or standard meetings created by users assigned this policy.

claims.where: controls[1].ui
claims.claim: Template visibility is configured at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting template policies > policy > Edit > Viewable templates > template > Hide.
claims.quote:
In the Teams admin center, expand Meetings and select Meeting template policies.
2. Select the policy you want to change, and then select Edit.
3. To make a viewable template hidden, select the template in the Viewable templates list and then select Hide.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout
claims.claim: Admins can create and adjust custom templates with locked, hidden or editable options in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote:
Use this procedure to create a custom meeting template in the Teams admin center.

claims.where: Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The governance checklist names controls that have no corresponding table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Create the custom template', 'publish any sensitivity label', 'Check the Copilot setting', 'Assign the policy'. Table: 'Which custom meeting template is the default' and 'Which meeting templates users in a policy can see'.
claims.fix: The checklist steps for creating or adjusting template options, publishing sensitivity labels, checking the Copilot meeting policy and assigning the policy lack corresponding controls-table rows. Remove those checklist steps rather than adding unverified rows.

claims.where: Governance controls: Copilot controls
claims.claim: The template's Copilot option and the Teams meeting policy's Copilot setting are separate controls, and the known issue belongs to the meeting policy.
claims.quote: This issue is related to the Copilot meeting policy and not the default meeting template.
